ARCHIVE.md.C-AR-OLD-CLOTHES: Not rare, and not Danish. One line each, with no claim that any is wrong — only that each has a membership rule doing one job and an attribution doing another: - Citizenship. A determinate legal status, acquired by birth, descent or naturalisation. Used as a proxy for population, culture, ancestry, or behaviour — none of which the membership rule tracks. The rule is *legal*; the attribution is usually *biological or cultural*. - Race. The literature's central dispute is exactly this statistic. Lewontin (1972) partitioned human genetic variance: ~85% within populations, ~15% between — an ICC of 0.15. Edwards (2003) replied that correlated loci make classification accurate anyway, which is true and is *our compact-null finding*: high classifiability is what a smooth cline gives you wherever you cut it. Rosenberg et al. (2002) is cited for finding clusters; Serre & Pääbo (2004) sampled the same geography continuously and got gradients. Sampling design, again. - Species. Biological, morphological and phylogenetic species concepts are three different membership rules over the same organisms, and they do not agree. Which one is "correct" has no answer; which one predicts a given trait does. - Industrial sector (SIC, NACE). A firm's code is assigned, often by the firm. Productivity and emissions are then compared "within sector". - Diagnosis codes. A membership rule built for billing, used as a phenotype. - Deprivation by postcode. An area statistic attributed to the individuals in it — which is the ecological fallacy, and the same error AREAS.md reports for Denmark

AREAS.md.C-AR-ASSIGN: Assignment is by nearest point on the marine boundary, one rule for every layer, with the largest distance kept for each layer in each area and anything beyond 20 km dropped.
AREAS.md.C-AR-CUMHOC: A national time series has one unit of replication. The water bodies with two or more bathing stations number 65, so an effect size can be estimated across them.
AREAS.md.C-AR-CUMHOC-DESIGN: This sets bathing-water quality against sewage pressure — outfall, treatment-plant and basin density per km² — because both sides of that pair exist per area. It is **cum hoc**: a correlation across places at one time, with no control for coast type, flushing, or population.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ENCLOSURE: "Roskilde Fjord" is not an arbitrary line on a map, and it is worth saying so plainly before objecting to anything. It names a real hydrographic object: an inlet bounded by land that opens to the sea through Isefjorden. That is a **claim about enclosure**, it is physical, and it is true.
AREAS.md.C-AR-GAP-CLASSES: The distinction inside that table matters as much as the table. `closed` is a gap in the world's availability; `open_unassembled` is a gap in our effort and is nobody's fault but ours; `absent` is the only one where a search was run to the end, and even that is bounded by the search.
AREAS.md.C-AR-GAPS: **And the corpus is named together with what is missing from it.** A coverage figure has a numerator nobody can measure — the evidence that exists — so counting what we assembled gives a *lower bound on evidence* and therefore an *upper bound on absence*. That is only interpretable beside the terms we know belong in the numerator and cannot add. They are kept in `data/manual/coverage_gaps.json`, a hand-kept record, in three kinds:
AREAS.md.C-AR-HOMOGENEITY: The assessment then uses the same word to mean something else entirely: that a measurement taken anywhere in it stands for the whole of it. That is a **claim about homogeneity**, and it is statistical. One sense is about where the water is bounded; the other is about whether the water inside those bounds is alike. Nothing carries you from the first to the second, and the name does the carrying unnoticed because the same three words serve both.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ILTSVIND: In Denmark, oxygen below 4 mg/L is called iltsvind.
AREAS.md.C-AR-LIFT-RULE: A partition's value is not how well it predicts, but **how much better it predicts than its own shape alone would**.
AREAS.md.C-AR-MODEL-MATCH: **The model flag follows DHI's list.** A water body counts as modelled when DHI's 2015 method report lists it among the water bodies with a station-level statistical model, matched to this layer by DHI's water-body number, with every name read against the layer's own (`data/manual/statistical_models.json`). One of DHI's models covers five Limfjord bredninger together, so all five are counted; one water body it lists, Randers Fjord's Grund Fjord, is not in the marine layer used here.
AREAS.md.C-AR-NAMED-CORPUS: So absence is reported here as a count over a named corpus, and the corpus is named every time.
AREAS.md.C-AR-NEITHER: Counted with that flag, 46 water bodies covering 24,359 km² (56% of Danish sea) carry neither the flag nor a repeated observation **in the two layers counted here** — bathing water, and the hazardous-substance layer, which holds no marine point.
AREAS.md.C-AR-NOT: It is not a causal model per area. It is the ledger you need before you can build one: which areas have enough observation to support a claim, which have none, and over which years each stream exists — so that an analysis published in 2025 cannot quietly rest on a relation fitted to 1990–2012 without a reader seeing the gap.
AREAS.md.C-AR-NOT-PERCENT: **Those are counts, and they are deliberately not percentages.** Saying *8% of the sea has no long observation* would be the missing-denominator error this project exists to point at. The denominator is known — the sea is 43,579 km². The numerator is not, because it is the extent of an absence, and an absence can only be measured against a search that was exhaustive. Ours was ODA plus two layers; ICES and EMODnet sit outside it, and so does whatever university, municipal or unpublished series exist.
AREAS.md.C-AR-NULLS: The three nulls answer three different questions. **Shuffled** permutes station labels while keeping basket sizes, so it destroys geography and keeps the size structure. **Latitude stripes** are equal-count horizontal bands, as many as there are real baskets, so they keep compactness and equal sizes but ignore hydrography. **Size- and shape-matched** baskets have the same size distribution as the real ones and are grown from random seeds by nearest neighbour, three times over, so they are compact blobs of the right sizes following no hydrography at all — the only control that varies one thing at a time.
AREAS.md.C-AR-PART-STAT: A partition is not right or wrong in general; it is predictive *for a variable*. So the question is what the water bodies encode. The statistic, computed within month by `scripts/partition_score.py`, is a **ratio of mean squares**: the between-basket mean square over the sum of the between- and within-basket mean squares. One means stations in the same basket agree completely. With labels that carry no information both mean squares estimate the same variance and the ratio sits near one half, not zero — so no value in the table below can be read on its own, only its difference from a null.
AREAS.md.C-AR-PHYSICS: **And where exchange is restricted, the physics runs against the transfer, not with it.** Restricted exchange is what *preserves* a gradient. A basin with freshwater entering at its head and little exchange at its mouth holds salinity, residence-time and oxygen gradients along its length because it does not flush; open water erases such differences by mixing. So the better the enclosure, the weaker the homogeneity assumption becomes: the two senses **pull in opposite directions**, and the enclosures that most deserve their names are the ones least entitled to be treated as single units.
AREAS.md.C-AR-POSITION: The practical rule that follows, and the reason the station-level series exist: **the unit of observation is a position.** Everything else — this page included — is an aggregate computed inside somebody's polygon, and should be read as a statement about that polygon as much as about the sea.
AREAS.md.C-AR-PULS: **PULS is the sharpest case.** It holds the per-event overflow volumes that B1 calls the single most valuable missing series — volumes that are themselves largely modelled, by this project's source register — and an access attempt with a private MitID was refused because no CVR or VAT number attached to it was valid, so this is not a login anyone has neglected to perform. Access appears to require a registered business or authority, in which case a private citizen cannot obtain it.
AREAS.md.C-AR-READING: One reading fits these numbers, and it is not tested here: if salinity is spatially smooth, any compact grouping predicts it well (0.844 from random blobs) and the real boundaries have little left to add; if oxygen is spatially rough, blobs do poorly and boundaries that follow enclosure carry real information.
AREAS.md.C-AR-RECORD: The full record for each area — every pressure, every stream with its years, and the written-out list of what cannot be modelled there — is in `data/derived/areas.json`, which `scripts/areas.py` writes locally and the repository does not ship, and drawn with its timeline on [the map](areas.html).
AREAS.md.C-AR-REGISTER: ODA's station register holds **6,258 positioned marine stations**.
AREAS.md.C-AR-REQUIREMENT: A requirement does not wait for either: in the method behind the second water plans, every one of its 119 water bodies was given an indsatsbehov, whether it had a statistical model or not.
AREAS.md.C-AR-REVERSAL: Against the matched blobs the ordering **reverses**: surface oxygen saturation gains most (+0.402), surface salinity little (+0.124), and fluorescence's lift is below zero (-0.050) — but the three blob runs themselves spread by 0.109 for fluorescence, so for it the official partition does no better than random compact blobs, and whether it does worse is not shown.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ROSK-HALVES: **And the two halves fail on different variables.** The inner fjord's stations disagree for oxygen (0.65) and agree for salinity (0.29); the outer fjord's are the reverse — close for oxygen (0.25), apart for salinity (0.87). Within this one fjord, a boundary drawn to serve one variable does not serve the other. That is one case, not a proof about every partition; it is the case `X22` would test systematically.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ROSK-METHOD: The station-level series make this checkable rather than arguable. Both halves of Roskilde Fjord carry several stations, so for any month where 3 or more measured, the disagreement *between* stations can be set against the variation *across* months. *Spread between stations* is the population standard deviation across the stations in a month, averaged over the months, beside the median range; *spread across months* is the standard deviation of the monthly means.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ROSK-OXY: **The inner fjord's own stations disagree about bottom oxygen by a median of 3.35 mg/l within a single month.** A spread that size is most of the distance from zero to that threshold, so in a month when the fjord's bottom water is near it, one station can read below and another above — and whether that body "has iltsvind" can then depend on which of its own stations is read. The ratio puts it another way: the spread between stations is **65% of the spread of the monthly means across months**.
AREAS.md.C-AR-ROSK-SOURCE: Computed by `scripts/station_places.py` from `docs/data/areas/stations_series.*`, which carry no partition at all — the water-body assignment used here is loaded separately from `station_waterbody_overlay.json`, on purpose, so that using it is a deliberate act.
AREAS.md.C-AR-SAME-WIDTH: **Same width — an exact statement is fine, including of an absence.** *None of the 123 water bodies has a marine point in the national hazardous-substance layer: its 256 points are 152 lake and 104 river.* The category is that layer and the count is of all of it, so its complement is exact.
AREAS.md.C-AR-SAMPLED: One further limit bounding every row: stations are not placed at random and are far denser in some baskets than others, so this scores the partition *as sampled*. It cannot distinguish a well-drawn basket from one whose stations happen to sit close together.
AREAS.md.C-AR-SCOPE: This page refuses the aggregate. One record per marine water body: what presses on it, what is observed in it, **over which years each of those streams exists**, and what cannot be modelled there.
AREAS.md.C-AR-SERIES-COVERAGE: The part of it this page can place in water bodies is the station series behind the partition tests below — 1,415 stations with a monthly record, 1,313 of them inside a water body by point in polygon — and **119 of the 123 water bodies contain at least one of those.** Counted over that series: 4 water bodies contain no station with data in 2 or more distinct years, 10 water bodies contain no station with data in 5 or more distinct years, 12 water bodies contain no station with data in 10 or more distinct years.
AREAS.md.C-AR-SPLIT-UNSTATED: The documents this project holds give the general basis for water bodies' boundaries — the water framework directive asks member states to set them, and the plans sort coastal waters into types with a catchment each — but none of them says why this fjord is two units rather than one or three, or what measurement would settle it.
AREAS.md.C-AR-TABLE-KEY: `model` — a DHI statistical model, as described above (DCE fitted its statistical models on 1990–2012). `bath` — bathing stations, and the years they span. `r` — the mean correlation between the yearly classes of a water body's informative bathing stations, where there are three or more. `RBU` — rain-conditioned outfalls. `PE` — approved treatment-plant load. `gaps` — the number of written-out reasons this area cannot be modelled.
AREAS.md.C-AR-THREE-RANKINGS: **The result depends almost entirely on what it is compared against, and three reasonable comparisons give three different rankings.**
AREAS.md.C-AR-TWO-UNITS: The partition half-concedes this without following it through. Roskilde Fjord appears here as two water bodies, `DKCOAST1` (ydre, 71 km²) and `DKCOAST2` (indre, 52 km²) — an admission that one enclosure is at least two units.
AREAS.md.C-AR-WIDER: **Category wider than corpus — only a count is honest.** *56% of the sea has no marine observation* would name a category — marine observation — far wider than the two layers actually searched, and report the leftover after subtracting what we happened to find as though it were measured, which is the operation [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md) is about.
AREAS.md.C-AR-WINNERS: Against the shuffle, salinity gains most, by a distance; against the stripes, surface oxygen saturation does.
AREAS.md.C-AR-WITHIN-MONTH: Within month is essential. Every station in Denmark shares a season, so pooling across months puts the seasonal signal into the between-basket term and makes every partition look excellent, including an absurd one.
AREAS.md.C-AR-X22: A boundary drawn inside a fjord is a hypothesis about where the water changes, and it can be tested: `X22` in [EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md) sets out how, using pairs of measurements at matched separation either side of a line.

CATEGORY.md.C-AR-ATTRIBUTION: **An attribution.** What members are taken to share. This is a *statistical* claim, and nothing in the membership rule establishes it.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-CAT-COMPANION: This is the companion to [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md), and the same shape of mistake one column to the left. That page is about a *number* nobody measured being treated as one. This is about a *category* nobody measured being treated as one.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-CITIZENSHIP: **Citizenship.** A legal status, acquired by the routes a country's law sets out. It can be used as a proxy for population, culture, ancestry, or behaviour — none of which the membership rule tracks. The rule is *legal*; the attribution is *biological or cultural*.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-CONDITION: **Condition on what everything shares.** Every marine station in Denmark experiences the same season. Pool across months and the seasonal signal lands in the between-basket term and *every* partition scores well — including a deliberately absurd one. The same applies wherever a common driver exists: compare within year, within cohort, within whatever the members hold in common regardless of basket.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-DEFECT: The measurement above has a defect that has to be stated before the worked example, because it applies to every number on this page.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-DEMAND: If the answer to the third is unknown, the category is being used as data when it is a model, and any figure computed inside it is a statement about the basket at least as much as about the world.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-DIFFERENCE: A circular statistic compared against a *shape-matched null* stops being circular, because the null partitions were not chosen to be real. Each number separately depends on the assumption; the **difference** between them measures what the chosen partition adds. That is the argument for the exercise below, and it is why a single reported value — a bare $F_{\mathrm{ST}}$, a bare intraclass correlation, a bare $R^2$ between groups — cannot by itself say whether the groups are anything.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-ESTIMATORS: Nor is it one statistic. After Wright's, papers gave differing definitions and estimators, and published estimates for the same pairs of populations have moved more than twofold with the estimation method, the way estimates are combined across loci and the choice of loci. It is an aggregation function over a chosen metric, presented as an observable.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-FST-CIRCLE: **The intraclass correlation takes the partition as an input.** So does $F_{\mathrm{ST}}$, a statistic of the same family in population-genetics clothing: $F_{\mathrm{ST}} = (H_T - H_S)/H_T$, and $H_S$ — the variation *within subpopulations* — cannot be computed until the subpopulations have been declared. Citing an $F_{\mathrm{ST}}$ value as evidence that populations are distinct therefore assumes what it sets out to show, unless it is set against what partitions not chosen to be real would give.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-ICC-FAMILY: There is a standard family of statistics for this: the **intraclass correlation** and its relatives. Pick two members of the population at random. If they are in the same basket, how much more alike are they than two picked without regard to basket? For the intraclass correlation, one means membership tells you everything and zero means it tells you nothing. The scores this project computes are a relative — a ratio of mean squares, on which no information reads near one half rather than zero — which is one more reason to read only their difference from a null.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-ICD: **Diagnosis codes.** For more than a century the basis for comparable statistics on causes of death and disease, and now also used for resource allocation and reimbursement — a membership rule built for counting, used to stand for a condition.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-LIFT-RULE: **A partition's value is not how well it predicts, but how much better it predicts than its own shape alone would.**
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-MEMBERSHIP: **A membership rule.** Who is in. This is usually sound, often precise, and frequently a genuine fact about the world. Roskilde Fjord really is an enclosure. Danish citizenship really is a determinate legal status. A postcode really is a postcode.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-NO-ERRORBAR: **Not one of them has an error bar, and not one of them was measured.** Each is the output of a model — a polygon someone drew, a legal test someone applied, a classification someone wrote down — presented in the same table, in the same typeface, as the quantities that came off an instrument. The instrument reading is an observation with a known error. The category is a claim with an unstated one.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-NULL-CONDITIONED: A null answers: **given these measurements, does this grouping beat chance?** The answer is still conditioned on which measurements were taken, so it cannot separate a property of the entities from an artifact of what someone chose to record.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-NULL-LIMIT: The null comparison above is not the strongest test available. It is the strongest test available *when the feature space is small*.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-OWN-EXAMPLE: This page's own worked example sits below that threshold — 9 variables, so 4 per half, and far from independent: oxygen and its saturation, the same quantity at two depths — which is why the marine result is suggestive only. The method wants a case with dozens of characters per entity, which is what `../organism` exists to try.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-POSTCODE: **Deprivation by postcode.** An area statistic attributed to the individuals in it — which is the ecological fallacy, and the same error [AREAS.md](AREAS.md) reports for Denmark.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-QUESTION: The name serves both functions, so the switch between them goes unnoticed. Asking "is this a real category?" answers the first question and is almost always yes. The question that has content is different:
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-RACE: **Race.** A dispute in the literature turns on exactly this statistic. By Edwards's account it is often stated, after Lewontin in 1972, that about 85% of human genetic variation lies within populations and only 15% between them. Edwards (2003) replied that the information distinguishing populations lies in the correlations between loci, so classification can be accurate anyway — the shape of the compact-null finding above, where compact groupings of a smooth field score well wherever they are cut. Rosenberg et al. (2002) found clusters without using the individuals' origins; Serre & Pääbo (2004), sampling individuals homogeneously across the globe, found gradients rather than discrete clusters. Sampling design, again.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-READING: One reading fits these numbers, and it is not tested here: if salinity is spatially smooth, *any* compact grouping predicts it well and real boundaries have little left to add; if oxygen is rough, shape alone fails and boundaries that follow enclosure carry real information.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-RESCUE: **This is why the null is not a refinement. It is the thing that rescues the measurement.**
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-REVERSAL: Only the third varies one thing at a time, and against it the ordering from the first **reverses** — oxygen saturation gains most, salinity little — and fluorescence's lift is below zero but inside the spread of the three blob runs, so for fluorescence the official partition does no better than random compact blobs.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SAMPLING: The partition can come from the **sampling design** itself. Collect fifty Danes and fifty Dutch and "Danish" and "Dutch" are your groups by construction; the statistic then reports on a boundary the fieldwork drew.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SECTOR: **Industrial sector** (SIC, NACE). A code attached to each firm from a classification; productivity and emissions can then be compared "within sector".
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SELF-APPLY: this project sorts 166 mechanisms into 17 groups, which is a partition it has not scored either.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SHAPE-NULL: **Compare against a null that matches the basket's shape.** This is the part that gets skipped, and skipping it is how a defensible number comes out backwards.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SMALL-SPACE: A feature space of three or four measurements cannot be split into disjoint halves: there is nothing to hold out, and a null is the only test available.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SPECIES: **Species.** Species concepts agree that a species is a separately evolving lineage but disagree about which further property makes one — reproductive isolation, diagnosability, monophyly — so the same organisms can be sorted differently. Which concept to use is argued over; which one predicts a given trait is a question with an answer.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-SPLIT-TEST: A grouping that appears only when one particular measurement is included is an artifact of that measurement. A grouping that appears whichever features are drawn is a property of the entities. Convergence as the subsets widen is the signal; flat agreement near chance means there is nothing to converge on. The official partition is then scored on the same axis — its agreement with each derivation — so it is one candidate among them rather than the standard they are marked against.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-TELL: Open the Danish marine monitoring archive this project holds. Its measured columns come with what a measurement comes with: a sonde serial number, a sampling instrument, an analysis method, a laboratory, a quality level, and a mark for a value below what the method could detect.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-THRESHOLD: **So the rule is a threshold, not a preference.** Below 12 independent features — a judgment, stated as one — use a shape-matched null and accept that it cannot distinguish the entities from the instrument. Above that, split the feature space, because you can.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-TWO-THINGS: Every basket carries two things that are easy to conflate, and the conflation is the whole problem:
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-WHERE-MANY: Where many measurements accumulate on the same entities, the stronger test is available and the weaker one is a habit.
CATEGORY.md.C-AR-WINNERS: The winners are read from the scores, and the first two disagree, not marginally: surface oxygen saturation gains **+0.065** over the shuffle and **+0.408** over the stripes, while against the shuffle salinity gains most.

DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-AREAS: Extracted flooded area: Bispebjerg 2.22 km², KBH Vest 1.39, Amager 1.18, Ladegårdsåen 0.42, Nørrebro 0.36, Østerbro 0.10, Indre By 0.04.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-AXIS: **Gotcha:** asked in WFS `1.0.0` this server returns `EPSG:4326` as `[lon, lat]`, and `1.1.0` flips the axis order. `scripts/common.py` detects which arrived rather than trusting either.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-BGV: **`bgv_type` decoding** is in `data/manual/codelists.json`, from Miljøstyrelsen's [Datateknisk anvisning DP02 v4 (2024)](https://mst.dk/media/bnkdidho/dta-dp02-rbu-version-4-2024.pdf). Its table of the data PULS requires for combined-sewer overflows defines `OV`, `OS`, `OF`, `OK`, `Bypass` and `Skybrud`; its list for separate-sewer outfalls defines `SE` (separate rainwater) and `SF` (separate rainwater with a detention basin), which make up 487 of our 680 points.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-BORROW: **Lending a clock, with a caveat.** If a station-day is one moment — which is assumed, not checked — the clock can be lent from `kemi` to `ctd`, the only route in the data held to putting a time on oxygen at depth. `scripts/depth_clock.py` does it through `scripts/clock.py`, lending only a `kemi` clock that is an observed time: 4,688,007 CTD oxygen measurements are placed that way, and 2,454,520 have no usable clock to borrow. The first count is taken after the script's quality filters and the second before them, so the two are not shares of one population.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-BOTTOM: In `maaledybde`, `BundDybde_m` reaches 2300 m at `Læsø rende`, where the station's 510 readings have a median of 22.565 m, and 292.3 m at a station named `Hirtshals 15 m`, whose readings have a median of 17.5 m.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-CENSOR: **Censoring hidden behind column names that do not say so.** `ResultatAttribut` is `<` on 85,035 `kemi` rows, where `Resultat` holds *the detection limit, not the measurement* — read as a value it biases the parameter high.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-CKAN: The city's CKAN catalogue answers at `https://admin.opendata.dk/api/3/action/package_search?q=organization:city-of-copenhagen`; the same path on `www.opendata.dk` answered `404`.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-CLIP: Layers here are national, so `fetch_wfs.py` clips them — by `komm_navn` where that column exists, otherwise by bounding box; the layers without a municipality column would come back empty without the bounding-box fallback.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-CLOCKPY: Every analysis that places a water-chemistry sample in time takes the instant from `scripts/clock.py`, which returns one UTC instant or says why there is none.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-CORNER: So a modelled depth at a street corner is never checked against the water actually standing there.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-DETLIMIT: The same chapter asks for values below the detection limit to be reported as measured, not as zero or as the limit with `<`. Yet 72,026 of the 1,153,832 nutrient, TOC and POC rows in `kemi` carry `<` — though which rows were sampled under this chapter the archive cannot say, since `TekniskAnvisningAnvendt` carries one value throughout.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-DHM: `scripts/terraincheck.py` fetches the national elevation model's terrain (`dhm_terraen`) from Dataforsyningen's WCS, `https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/dhm_wcs_DAF`, with a token kept on this machine and at the resolution it asks for, to check the 2012 flood sheets against the ground.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-DP02-CALIB: Miljøstyrelsen's technical standard (dTA DP02) calibrates a model on measurement *at the overflow structure*: at least five clearly separable overflow events must be in the measured data.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-EMPTYCOLS: **Columns that carry nothing.** `TekniskAnvisningAnvendt` is single-valued across every row of the three extracts that carry it, and `Afsluttet` across both that carry it, so neither can be used to filter for protocol compliance.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-ENUMS: `scripts/enums.py` counts every distinct value of every column of `kemi` and `ctd`, and `scripts/ds_facts.py` counts the traps below over every row of all four, because reading the top few values of a column is how a rare sentinel survives.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-FLOOD-PDFS: It is published as **7 raster PDFs** — amager, bispebjerg, indre-by, kbhvest, ladegaardsaaen, norrebro, osterbro — from 8 to 30 MB each, an orthophoto with the depth bands painted over it. The dataset record says the calculations are from 2012, and each sheet's title puts the event in 2010.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-FLOOD-UNUSABLE: This is the most important thing in this catalogue and the least usable. Where rain ponds in Copenhagen was calculated at municipal scale and published as an image: no coordinates this project could use, no vector extents, no depth values - so nothing can be overlaid, intersected or queried until each sheet is placed and read.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-FLOOD-WHAT: `Oversvømmelsesscenarier for vandoplande` on opendata.dk: flood scenarios from the city's cloudburst plans for each water catchment, based on calculations, for a 100-year event, banded `0.05-0.1 m` / `0.1-0.2 m` / `0.2-0.5 m` / `0.5-1 m` / `1-2 m` / `>2 m`. Which model produced them, over what terrain, is not stated.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-FLOWINPUT: It is also the input for **modelling where rain flows**: fill the terrain's sinks, compute flow direction and accumulation, and surface flow paths and ponding depressions come out directly, rather than being inferred from the plan.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-HOFOR: The utility. Its page for contractors sends requests for pipe information to LER, and `hofor.dk` is used here as a citation source for the manual register of structures, not as a data source.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-INTEGRATED: **Sample type decides what a depth means.** The technical instruction's sampling chapter ([Kap. 5](https://ecos.au.dk/fileadmin/ecos/Fagdatacentre/Marin/TA_NOVA_1998/Kap05.doc)) prescribes integrated samples over 0–10 m, over 0–25 m, or down to the depth of the photic zone. In `kemi`, 2,261 of the 9,734 `Dybdeintegreret prøve` rows carry a nominal depth of 3 m or less and will enter a surface filter as though they were point measurements. An integral is not a measurement at its midpoint.
DATA_SOURCES.md.C-DS-INTRO: What is public, what needs an account, what does not exist in open form, and what each thing is good for. Everything marked **fetched** is pulled by the scripts in `scripts/` and lands in `data/raw/`. METHOD_LAB.md.C-DEPTH-BORROW: 4,688,007 oxygen measurements at depth were placed in time with a clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry bottle, and 2,454,520 had no bottle with a usable time to borrow from - none that day, or one whose clock is a filled-in default or of a mixed convention. The two counts are not shares of one population: the first is counted after `scripts/depth_clock.py`'s quality filters and the second before them.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-DIURNAL-BOUND: A cycle of size 0.7 mg/l produces a spread at least as large as the observed one in 100% of draws, and every smaller size on the grid does so in fewer than 95% of them. So if the real surface cycle follows the sine of the sun's elevation, its size is below 0.7 mg/l. The size is the coefficient on that sine: the swing from night to noon it would give where the sun stands overhead, and more than the swing on any Danish day.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-ASSUMPTION-FREE: The same samples, stations and seasons are compared with themselves, only the hour redrawn, so no model of the sea's mean state or seasons enters. What does enter is the stipulated sun-shaped cycle and Gaussian noise of the measured size, against a round-the-clock schedule with the hour drawn uniformly; a cycle peaking at another hour would lose a different share.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-BORROW-ARTEFACT: If casts systematically precede bottles, any diurnal pattern found at depth is partly an artefact of the borrowing.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-BOUND-STRONGER: A bound is a stronger object than a null: a null cannot separate *the effect is absent* from *the instrument could not have seen it*, and a bound can.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-CATCHMENT-RULE: The same will hold for official catchment delineations when this project's own flow model is scored against them: agreement will be a sanity check, not a validation.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-CIRC-INTRO: Each item below is a way a check on this project's methods can pass without testing what it seems to test. The failure is silent: a circular check passes.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-CLOCK-KINDS: `Startklok` is not UTC wherever that can be tested, and it is not one kind of thing. `scripts/clockzone.py` compares every station with itself in the weeks either side of each summer-time change: a wall clock does not move, a UTC clock jumps an hour one way, a clock with the offset added jumps the other. Until the late nineties the archive's times are Danish wall-clock times with the offset *added*, mixed with filled-in defaults that read noon and three in the morning local once the offset is taken off; from the early two-thousands they are wall-clock times; and some suppliers' conventions are mixed.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-CLOCKPY: Every analysis that places a water-chemistry sample in time takes the instant from `scripts/clock.py`, which returns one UTC instant or says why there is none; the raw column is read elsewhere only for fixed readings kept as controls and a clock-hour count no page uses.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-DCE-MEAN: DCE report a mean $R^2$ of 0.56 across their models.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-DCE-METHOD: DCE choose each model's variables by stepwise, cross-validated regression on a calibration part of the data, offering each candidate - nutrient and freshwater inputs, wind, light, salinity, stratification, temperature - over up to 43 period windows. They set the number of variables by weighing calibration against validation performance, evaluate the model on held-out data, refit it on all the data, and accept it on several criteria, of which an $R^2$ of at least 0.4 is one.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-DCE-SCOPE: [OBSERVING.md](OBSERVING.md) examines the statistical models DCE built to calculate how far nutrient inputs must fall for Danish fjords and coastal waters to reach good ecological status, at 29 coastal monitoring stations representing 22 water bodies.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-DEPTHCLOCK-CHECK: `scripts/depth_clock.py` therefore uses supplied field-sheet times where they exist and, where a cast has both a supplied and a borrowed time, reports the distribution of the offset between them - so supplied times check the borrowed clock as well as replacing it. Until such times exist it reports the check as not run, instead of reporting an unchecked number as a result.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-FLOOD-MODEL: The 2012 Copenhagen sheets are calculated flood scenarios for a hundred-year event, published by Københavns Kommune: the output of a model, not a record of flooding. Which model, over what terrain, and whether it included the sewers, is not stated in anything this project holds.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-FLOW-VS-FLOOD: Scoring a terrain-driven flow model against them measures agreement with another model, not correctness against the world, so they can serve as a sanity check and not as truth.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-LEFT-OUT: Left out: 18,717 samples whose clock is a filled-in default and 10,198 from suppliers whose clock convention is mixed. Neither can be placed against the sun.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-LICENSE: So the objection worth taking seriously is not *this method has no precedent*. It is the narrower one: **a simulation on its own licenses claims about the instrument, not about the world.** A claim about the world needs a measurement: the bound below is the real archive's spread read through the simulation, and it holds only under the simulation's assumptions. The table at the end lists instances. The build refuses a number built on simulation on any page but a method page; prose is not checked.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-METHOD: `scripts/detectable.py` takes the **62,069 surface-oxygen samples** the real estimate uses - read through `cycles.read_samples()`, so with the same filters and the same clock - imposes a cycle proportional to the sine of the sun's elevation at each sample's instant and place, adds noise measured from the archive, and runs the estimator itself: `cycles.deviations()`, with its window and sun bins, and one rule, applied to both sides, for which bins count. Each size is run on 40 noise draws, the round-the-clock comparison on fewer. It claims nothing about how the sea behaves. It asks only: *if it behaved this way, at this size, would this schedule have found out?*
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NEIGHBOURS: The estimator sees a diurnal signal only through contrast *within* a station's own ±10-day window. Of the 62,069 samples, **64% have no other sample from their station inside that window** and contribute nothing. Of the 22,571 that do, **11,244 - 50% - have neighbours only in their own sun-elevation bin**, and so add no contrast between bins. Whatever this estimator can say about the daily cycle rests on the rest.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NOISE-CIRC: The bound above depends on an estimate of the noise the estimator must see through. Taken as the archive's within-cell residual spread, that estimate would contain whatever diurnal signal exists, so a large real cycle would inflate the yardstick used to rule a large real cycle out - and a noisier null reaches the observed spread more often, so the bias would favour this page's conclusion that the spread is not a cycle.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NOISE-FLOOR: Under that condition the median best $R^2$ from pure noise is 0.56–0.66, and 82–90% of noise models clear an $R^2$ of 0.4.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NOISE-MEASURED: Noise is measured from the archive, at **0.8427 mg/l**, from 11,244 samples whose window neighbours all share their sun bin, so the contrast between bins cannot enter it; its Gaussian form is stipulated.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NOISE-NOW: The noise is therefore taken only from samples whose window neighbours all fall in their own sun-elevation bin, so only the diurnal variation inside one bin can enter it.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-NOT-FALSE: None of this shows that DCE's relations are false.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-ONE-ESTIMATOR: The two are compared through one estimator called on both sides: the observed spread and every synthetic recovery come from `cycles.deviations()`, with the same window, the same sun bins and the same rule for which bins count, over 40 noise draws per amplitude.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-OSSE: Building a known world, sampling it the way the real instrument samples, and checking whether the analysis recovers what was put in, is an established method. In meteorology and oceanography it is an **Observing System Simulation Experiment**: a *nature run* stands in for the world, synthetic observations are drawn from it with realistic error, and the analysis is scored against a truth that is known because it was constructed. The experiment below is one in miniature.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-OSSE-THEIRS: OSSEs are widely used to evaluate future observing systems and network designs ([Fujii et al., *Frontiers in Marine Science*, 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2019.00417/full)).
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-POWER: The same logic under another name is prospective power analysis - sizing an experiment by what it could detect, before it is run - which clinical-trial guidelines require ([the ICH guideline on statistical principles for clinical trials](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/ich-e-9-statistical-principles-clinical-trials-step-5_en.pdf)).
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-R2-NO-EVIDENCE: An $R^2$ of 0.4 is no hurdle for the simplified search on autocorrelated noise, which clears it more often than not. Whether DCE's reported $R^2$ carries evidence depends on whether it was measured on held-out data, which the report does not say; until that is known, this is a statement about a selection procedure, not about the water.
METHOD_LAB.md.C-ML-REPLICATION: The simulation below does not run that procedure. It runs a simpler one: an exhaustive search over every set of up to 3 of 8 candidates, 92 sets in all, scored by in-sample $R^2$, with no period windows, no cross-validation and no held-out data. The two simplifications pull in opposite directions: period windows would give noise more chances than this search does, while cross-validated selection and a held-out check would reject much of what an in-sample search accepts.
